newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF's Trichet urges businesses to invest.
newsitem.headline: BoF's Trichet urges businesses to invest.

text.p: Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet urged French businesses on Thursday to invest as financing conditions were exceptional and prospects for growth in Europe were real.

"I tell them it's the moment to invest," he told the French network LCI. "You'll regret afterwards not having invested. You have exceptional financing conditions and you have prospects for a rebound in European growth that are overall real."
He said France had the third-lowest interest rates in the world after Japan and Switzerland.
Trichet cited the 0.9 percent rise in France's third-quarter gross domestic product and forecasts by statistics agency INSEE for two percent 1996 growth year on year.
He said reports by economic institutes signalled that "we have passed the trough."
Trichet's upbeat tone echoed his comments in London on Wednesday that stronger growth was clearly under way in Europe and in France.
